Definition: adverb from G2570; well (usually morally):--(in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well.
BiblicalUsage: Kalos is 'well' — rightly, honourably, in a good way. Ye did run well, says Paul, who did hinder you; Peter says ye do well that ye take heed to the word as unto a light that shineth in a dark place; and the elders that rule well are counted worthy of double honour.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'well' is the word of a life well run. The race is run well when the word is heeded, the elders rule well, and the brethren are sent forward after a godly sort — and that is the standard I measure my own running by.
RelatedTopics: Good works; Leadership; Word of God
